title: Exceptions
content: In Angularity, JavaScript runtime errors are divided into two categories: Errors and Exceptions.

title: Exceptions
content: Exceptions are instances of the Exception class. They are expected to be caught and appropriately handled.Errors are all the errors that are not instances of Exception. They are regarded as critical errors that should never happen and typically breaks the application, such as TypeError. The occurrence of such an error implies something is wrong within the application that awaits fixes.

title: Exceptions
content: To create a type of exception, declare a class that extends from the Exception class.

title: Exceptions
content: Additional customizations can apply to add contextual properties or generate uniformed error messages:

title: Exceptions
content: It is worthy to note that both Exceptions and Errors are instances of Error. The way to distinguish them is instanceof Exception, not instanceof Error.

title: Exceptions
content: A recommended way to compose the catch block is to exhaust all the exceptions that are expected to be caught and re-throw the error if none of the exceptions are matched:

title: Exceptions
content: All Angularity libraries follow this convention for error handling, and it is recommended to also follow such convention in applications that uses Angularity.

title: AnimationAwareDialog
content: Currently, when closing a dialog, the corresponding overlay is immediately disposed, which means that the host element of the overlay is immediately removed from the DOM using the native API.

title: AnimationAwareDialog
content: The current behavior completely eliminated the possibility to implement a :leave animation for dialogs, since the ancestor element of the dialog, the overlay, is removed via the native DOM API, and the Angular animation engine cannot hook into this process to perform the :leave animation.

title: AnimationAwareDialog
content: This class works around the issue by waiting :leave animations to complete before disposing the overlay.

To avoid this situation, look into adding something like {@link timeout}, {@link take}, {@link takeWhile}, or {@link takeUntil} amongst others.
